name: George Soros
role: Investor and philanthropist; founder of the Open Society Foundations
summary: Soros advocates an open society built on political dissent, individual rights, and constitutional checks. He defends markets with public safeguards, favors European integration and international cooperation, and calls for rapid cuts in greenhouse-gas emissions.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He calls for military support to help Ukraine resist Russia’s invasion and treats armed defense as necessary to defeat it.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: His plan for stabilizing the euro relies on an active European Central Bank that buys bonds and protects debtor countries from default.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: He wants better cooperation between communities and police so that police can solve crimes and calls for reformers to maintain police funding.

abortion-legal.rationale: In a July 2022 Project Syndicate column he wrote that Congress must act, 'starting with protecting a woman's right to choose'.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: He praises Ukraine’s armed resistance to the Russian invasion and urges other countries to mobilize their resources to help defeat it.

assisted-dying.rationale: DuVivier documents his contribution to the campaign opposing repeal of the Oregon law authorizing physician-assisted dying for terminally ill adults.

capital-controls.rationale: In A New Global Financial Architecture he argues that restrictions on cross-border capital flows offer temporary relief but invite abuse and can destabilize open capital markets elsewhere.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: He argues that the global capitalist system can survive if public institutions deliberately address its instability and distributional problems.

common-currency.rationale: He argues for keeping the single European currency and proposes institutional changes to prevent the currency crisis from breaking up the union.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He grounds political sovereignty in the people and argues that any further transfer of powers to the European Union needs their authorization and accountability to their elected representatives.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: He co-founded the Roma Education Fund to counter longstanding educational exclusion and segregation of Roma children.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: He defends a European union of equals and criticizes the shift toward German control over the policies of debtor states.

democracy-best.rationale: In his Open Society lecture he prefers free elections and public criticism to enforced ideology, while saying that better policy judgments depend on the electorate’s willingness to confront evidence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: He describes political checks, rights of association and speech, and the ability to challenge abuse through the courts as essential to a functioning open society.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: His Open Society lecture treats competing interests and interpretations as essential to democratic checks, and at Davos he called for restoring a functioning two-party system in the United States.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He urges deep and rapid emissions reductions and proposes that developed governments jointly provide $100 billion in financing for climate mitigation in poorer countries.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He calls for liberal democracies to build a worldwide network of security alliances modeled on NATO.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: In discussing the expulsion of Roma, he expressly calls for equality before the law and rejects imputing criminal conduct to individuals on the basis of ethnicity.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He condemns organizing states around a dominant ethnicity and commends Bosnia and Macedonia for defending multiethnic states.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: He makes the case for a levy on currency trades and other financial transactions to offset the tax advantages of mobile financial capital, while favoring a separate financing proposal for immediate implementation.

force-without-un.rationale: In The Global Political Architecture he endorses the NATO intervention in Kosovo as a precedent for a democratic alliance acting against atrocities within a sovereign state, while criticizing the way it was carried out.

free-trade.rationale: He rejects the argument that globalization including free trade benefits everyone because the people and firms that gain seldom compensate those who lose.

gradual-change.rationale: He advocates improving imperfect institutions by trial and error and praises the European Union’s early method of pursuing successive limited objectives.

holocaust-denial.rationale: He recounts how Nazi occupation and deportations of Hungarian Jews to extermination camps forced his family and other Jews to survive in hiding.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: He attributes disruption of the global climate to human activity, emphasizing the large-scale release of carbon dioxide and methane.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: He calls for pursuing war-crimes prosecutions in Bosnia and condemns the international community for allowing the indicted Radovan Karadžić to remain politically active and evade justice.

islam-incompatible.rationale: He describes Sarajevo’s Muslim population as part of a cosmopolitan, tolerant society and rejects the prejudice that equates Islam with fanaticism.

limit-growth.rationale: He argues that strong carbon pricing and low-carbon investment can make climate action a source of new economic growth.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He rejects the theory that competitive markets deliver the best allocation of resources in practice, arguing that unregulated financial markets overshoot and cannot reliably correct their own mistakes.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: In The Global Political Architecture he argues that the Western response in Yugoslavia should have begun when Milošević revoked the autonomy of Kosovo and Vojvodina.

nation-first.rationale: He argues that the United States and other democracies should strengthen international cooperation even where states are tempted to prioritize their own immediate interests.

no-central-bank.rationale: His plan for keeping the euro relies on the European Central Bank intervening to stabilize credit conditions in the currency area.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: He endorses a negotiated two-state settlement in which Israel would withdraw from large parts of the West Bank in exchange for peace and recognition.

one-party-rule.rationale: He defends political competition and free elections and rejects enforcing a single political doctrine through state power.

open-borders.rationale: He calls for open internal EU borders while advocating that the EU maintain and protect its external borders and admit lawful migrants through an orderly process.

party-controls-media.rationale: He calls an independent press protected by law essential to citizens’ ability to hold rulers accountable.

person-over-state.rationale: He makes the protection of individual freedom the state’s purpose in an open society and rejects the closed-society principle that individuals exist to serve state rulers.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He presents the EU as an example of democratic states voluntarily giving up part of their sovereignty for shared purposes and describes his longstanding support for it.

population-transfer.rationale: He rejects the mass eviction and expulsion of Roma by European governments that claimed the group was a threat to public order.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: He urges liberal democracies to promote freedom and democracy in and around the security alliances they build.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He co-founded the Roma Education Fund, which supports efforts to end the segregation of Roma children in public schools.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He rejects closing Europe to refugees and economic migrants and advocates orderly admission of lawful migrants from outside Europe.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He calls for regulatory intervention against monopolies and stringent rules for dominant internet firms, while cautioning that banking regulations should be limited to what is needed.

religious-nation.rationale: He criticizes the use of a national Christian identity as a governing principle in Hungary and Poland and holds up Sarajevo’s coexistence of four religions as an example of an open society.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: He condemns the French expulsion of non-French Roma and argues that governments must not use ethnicity as a proxy for individual criminal conduct.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: He proposes changes to IMF lending and guarantees to reduce the advantages that countries at the center of the financial system enjoy over developing economies.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He urges wealthy countries to contribute their IMF reserve allocations to poverty alleviation, including by funding programs outside government channels where the local regime is repressive.

separated-powers.rationale: He defends constitutional checks that divide political power across branches and let each branch constrain the others, preventing absolute power.

social-market-economy.rationale: He calls a market economy a feature of an open society and argues for maintaining public social insurance against the instability of global markets.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He defines his ideal of open society by contrasting rule under law with rule by a single individual.

state-laws-apply-online.rationale: He calls for public authorities to regulate large online platforms as utilities in order to protect competition and access.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: His security program calls on the United States and other liberal democracies to take an active role in a network of NATO-style alliances.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He argues that citizens need enforceable rights to criticize and organize against those in power and that political dissent is essential to holding governments accountable.

tax-inheritance.rationale: He urges Congress to retain an estate tax that levied substantial sums on the largest estates and to spend its proceeds on people with fewer opportunities.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He agrees that the richest one percent should pay higher taxes and backs the Obama proposal to increase taxes on high earners.

taxation-theft.rationale: He defends the estate tax as an efficient and legitimate way of raising public revenue for people with fewer opportunities.

total-state.rationale: He explicitly rejects the closed-society model in which individuals serve the state and sees the state’s role as protecting individual freedom.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: He condemns ending food stamps and other federal assistance for lawful noncitizens and calls for equal treatment regardless of immigration status.

notes: Research covered economics, governing institutions, criminal justice, civil liberties, culture, migration, ecology, technology, international affairs, and methods of reform. Follow-up searches addressed religion and statehood, ethnic nationalism and minority rights, regional autonomy, and international security. Cannabis legalization and treatment for addiction are documented separately from general recreational-drug legalization. The author’s published excerpt from The Crisis of Global Capitalism and the mirror of its revised successor were reviewed.
